clue.text: Source of annoyance to a vixen, possibly

indicators.note: 'possibly' suggests one of several arrangements the letters could take

blocks.note: the three words supply the eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Something that would irritate a female fox.
explanation.walkthrough: VEXATION uses exactly the letters of TO A VIXEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A vexation is a thing that irritates or troubles someone, a cause of irritation.

clue.text: Close to Cadiz, unique area

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is wanted

blocks.note: last letter of the Spanish city's name
unique means the one and only

explanation.surface: A one-of-a-kind district near the Spanish port of Cadiz.
explanation.definitionFit: A zone is a region or district marked off from its surroundings.

clue.text: Action film doctor’s got into

indicators.note: something that has got into another thing sits inside it

blocks.note: a film is a thin covering layer, a coat
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification; the 's stands for 'has'

explanation.surface: A medic has landed a part in an action movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Action film' reads as a movie genre, but the clue splits after 'Action': film here is a thin layer, not a movie.
explanation.definitionFit: Combat is fighting, and military action means engagement with the enemy in battle.

clue.text: There’s always hardly any after fine plant

indicators.note: 'after' places the earlier-named words behind the later one in the answer

blocks.note: F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine
ever means always, as in 'ever hopeful'
few means hardly any

explanation.surface: A grumble that there is never much of a good plant to be had.
explanation.definitionFit: Feverfew is a daisy-like herb of the chrysanthemum family, once used against fevers and headaches.

clue.text: Stole fish, say, before beginning to grill something for breakfast, perhaps?

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter
'before' puts the first parts ahead of what follows

blocks.note: to poach is to take fish or game illegally
e.g. means 'for example', that is, say
opening letter of grill

explanation.surface: A poacher's tale: nicking a fish and putting it on the grill for the morning meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stole fish' looks like a crime followed by the cooking, but it all makes POACHED; the cooking sense of poach is the hidden pun.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg cooked in simmering water without its shell is a classic breakfast dish, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Mineral and two pints, followed by unknown quantity

indicators.note: 'followed by' sets the second part directly after the first

blocks.note: a quart is two pints
x, y and z are the unknowns of algebra

explanation.surface: A soft drink and a couple of pints, then who knows how many more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mineral' looks like mineral water ordered alongside pints of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Quartz is a hard crystalline silica found widely in rocks, a common rock-forming mineral.

clue.text: Major, OBE, lost bottle

indicators.note: letters that are lost have wandered out of order and must be rearranged

blocks.note: the rank and the honour supply the letters

explanation.surface: An army officer with an honour has mislaid his bottle, that is, his nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lost bottle' suggests losing one's nerve, British slang; here bottle is the definition. A jeroboam is a large champagne bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: A jeroboam is an oversized wine or champagne bottle holding about four standard bottles.

clue.text: Make most of large tent

indicators.note: 'most of' means everything except the final letter is kept

blocks.note: a marquee is a big tent for fêtes and weddings

explanation.surface: Instructions to put up nearly all of a big tent.
explanation.definitionFit: A marque is a brand of car or product, and make is used the same way, as in 'what make of car'.

clue.text: Used at sea to carry ten over in mass migration

indicators.note: being at sea means being confused, so the letters are jumbled
to carry something is to hold it within

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
X is the Roman numeral for ten
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Ships used to ferry people across the ocean in a great migration.
explanation.walkthrough: USED is rearranged to EDUS, and X plus O go inside after the E.
explanation.definitionFit: Exodus is the mass departure of a people, from the biblical flight of the Israelites from Egypt.

clue.text: Ornamental stone jardinière initially manufactured, first off

indicators.note: 'initially' asks for the opening letter only
'first off' means the leading letter is removed

blocks.note: opening letter of jardinière
manufactured means made

explanation.surface: An ornamental plant pot described as made of a decorative stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Jade is a hard green gemstone carved into ornaments and jewellery.

clue.text: Lorry can be deployed to deliver grain

indicators.note: deployed troops are spread out into new positions, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the three words supply the ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A truck may be sent out to bring in the harvested grain.
explanation.definitionFit: A barleycorn is a single grain of barley, also an old unit of length.

clue.text: Fate of king is settled

blocks.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
taken as written
a bill that is settled has been met

explanation.surface: A monarch's destiny has been decided.
explanation.definitionFit: Kismet is destiny, a word from Turkish via Arabic for one's allotted lot in life.

clue.text: Man in play perhaps trapping female criminal

indicators.note: trapping something means holding it inside

blocks.note: a man performing in a play is a male actor
F is the standard abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A stage actor holds a woman captive in a crime drama.
explanation.walkthrough: The female abbreviation slips into the gap between the two words of the phrase, not around the whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A malefactor is a wrongdoer, someone who commits a crime or does evil.

clue.text: Remove a restriction on a French band on the radio

indicators.note: something heard on the radio is judged by its sound, not its spelling

blocks.note: un is French for a
a frieze is a decorative band along a wall

explanation.surface: Lifting a ban on a French group being broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' looks like a pop group, but it is the strip of decoration on a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: To unfreeze assets or prices is to lift controls that had held them fixed.

clue.text: Hold and name the Spanish boy

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for name
el is Spanish for the
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: Instructions to keep and christen a Spanish lad.
explanation.definitionFit: A nelson is a wrestling grip in which an arm is locked behind the opponent's neck.

clue.text: Daughter, after working over staff, is held pending a hearing

indicators.note: 'after' places the first-named part at the end

blocks.note: a machine that is working is on
re means concerning, over as in 'a row over money'
to man a post is to staff it
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A daughter who was overworking her staff is now awaiting trial.
explanation.definitionFit: A prisoner on remand is kept in custody until the trial or next court appearance.

clue.text: Searches for people who’ll clean a chimney

blocks.note: first meaning: goes over an area thoroughly, as police do
second meaning

explanation.surface: Looking around for someone to clear the soot from a flue.
explanation.definitionFit: Police sweep a building when searching it, and chimney cleaners are called sweeps.

clue.text: Pelt nut, anti-establishment type

blocks.note: a pelt is an animal's skin
nut is slang for head

explanation.surface: A rebel pelting someone's head with a nut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pelt' looks like a verb, to throw things at, but it is the noun for a hide.
explanation.definitionFit: Skinheads were a shaven-headed youth subculture of 1960s Britain, rebellious against mainstream society.

clue.text: Inexperienced reporter interrupted by that girl, an angelic being

indicators.note: something interrupted has another thing put in its middle

blocks.note: a cub reporter is a novice journalist
her refers to a girl just mentioned

explanation.surface: A rookie journalist is cut off by a young woman of saintly character.
explanation.definitionFit: A cherub is a winged angel, in art often a chubby child, in scripture an order of heavenly being.

clue.text: With group on Scottish river, start on a journey

indicators.note: 'on' places one part next to the other in a down light or a sequence

blocks.note: a set is a group
the Forth flows into the Firth of Forth at Edinburgh

explanation.surface: A party of travellers beside a Scottish river, setting off.
explanation.definitionFit: To set forth is to depart or begin a trip, an old-fashioned phrasal verb.

clue.text: No time for article about cake

indicators.note: time is abbreviated T, and 'no' tells you to remove it
'about' suggests turning things around into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Too busy to write a piece about a pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: An éclair is a finger-shaped choux pastry filled with cream and topped with chocolate.

clue.text: Get back control across Georgia

indicators.note: a thing stretched across another encloses it

blocks.note: a rein controls a horse; to rein in is to control
GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

explanation.surface: Recovering power over the former Soviet republic.
explanation.definitionFit: To regain something is to recover possession of it after losing it.

clue.text: Motive in serious crime leader’s denied

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, and denying it takes it away

blocks.note: treason, betraying one's country, is among the gravest crimes

explanation.surface: A detective's line: the motive in a major crime that the ringleader denies.
explanation.definitionFit: A reason is the cause or grounds for an action, the same thing as a motive.

clue.text: Indication of disapproval mostly shown by one next to a police van

indicators.note: 'mostly' means all but the final letter is kept
'next to' sets the parts side by side

blocks.note: a black mark is a note of censure against someone
I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A frown of disapproval aimed at a person standing beside a police vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Black Maria is old British slang for a secure police vehicle used to carry prisoners.

clue.text: Long account by ambassador

blocks.note: AC is the abbreviation for account
an ambassador is styled His Excellency, HE

explanation.surface: A lengthy report written by a diplomat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like an adjective describing the account, but it is the verb: to long for something.
explanation.definitionFit: To ache for something is to yearn or long for it intensely.

clue.text: Assistant in a team, no saint

indicators.note: saint is abbreviated S, and 'no' says to remove it

blocks.note: taken as written
a side is a sports team

explanation.surface: A helper on a squad who is far from saintly.
explanation.definitionFit: An aide is a helper or assistant, especially to an important official.

clue.text: Deny any connection with row about pig

indicators.note: 'about' means going round, so one part surrounds the other

blocks.note: a din is a loud noise, a row
a sow is a female pig

explanation.surface: Washing your hands of a squabble over a pig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' rhymes with cow here: a racket, not a line.
explanation.definitionFit: To disown someone is to refuse to acknowledge them or accept any relationship.

clue.text: General behaviour in Manhattan thoroughfare

blocks.note: broad means general, as in 'in broad terms'
one's ways are one's habits or behaviour

explanation.surface: How an army general conducts himself on a New York street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General' looks like a military officer, but it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadway is the long avenue running through Manhattan, famous for its theatre district.
